title: Boss: the 3 a.m. log hunt
summary: Answer real incident questions from an nginx access log, the way grep, cut, sort, uniq and sed would.

steps.title: The pager went off
body: The site is slow. You have `access.log` in nginx's common format, one request per line, fields separated by single spaces:
Note the quotes stay attached: field 5 is `"GET`, field 7 is `HTTP/1.1"`. Field 8 is the status, field 9 is the response size.

steps.title: cut -d -f
steps.prompt: Write `List<string> Cut(List<string> lines, char delim, int field)` like `cut -d<delim> -f<field>` (1-based). A line with fewer fields gives the **whole line**, exactly as real cut does when the delimiter doesn't appear, and an empty string when it has the delimiter but not enough fields.
starter: List<string> Cut(List<string> lines, char delim, int field)
solution: List<string> Cut(List<string> lines, char delim, int field)
hints: `Split(delim)` keeps empty fields, which is what cut does with `a::b`.
Check `Contains(delim)` first for the whole-line rule.
template: Dojo.Eq("passwd users", new List<string> { "root", "ana" }, Cut(new List<string> { "root:x:0:0", "ana:x:1000:1000" }, ':', 1));
Dojo.Eq("empty field kept", new List<string> { "" }, Cut(new List<string> { "a::b" }, ':', 2));
Dojo.Eq("no delimiter: whole line", new List<string> { "nodelim" }, Cut(new List<string> { "nodelim" }, ',', 3));
Dojo.Eq("past the end", new List<string> { "" }, Cut(new List<string> { "a,b" }, ',', 5));

steps.title: Who is hammering us?
prompt: Write `List<string> TopIps(List<string> log, int n)`: the equivalent of
grep ' 5[0-9][0-9] ' access.log | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n N

That is: only lines whose **status field (8)** is a 5xx code; take the IP; count per IP; return the top `n` as `"<count> <ip>"`, highest first, ties broken by IP in ordinal order (that is what `sort` then a stable `sort -rn` gives).
hints: Split on single spaces; the status is index 7.
GroupBy IP, then order by count descending, then by IP.

steps.title: sed s///
prompt: Ops wants the log anonymised before you attach it to the ticket. Write `List<string> Sed(List<string> lines, string script)` supporting scripts of the form `s/PATTERN/REPLACEMENT/` and `s/PATTERN/REPLACEMENT/g`, where `PATTERN` is a regex. Without `g`, only the **first** match per line is replaced. You can assume `/` doesn't appear inside the pattern or replacement.
solution: return lines.Select(l => global ? re.Replace(l, parts[2]) : re.Replace(l, parts[2], 1)).ToList();
hints: `Regex.Replace(input, replacement, count)` on an instance limits the number of replacements.
template: var dojoIn = new List<string> { "10.0.0.7 hit 10.0.0.9", "no ip here" };
Dojo.Eq("first only", new List<string> { "x.x.x.x hit 10.0.0.9", "no ip here" }, Sed(dojoIn, "s/[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+/x.x.x.x/"));
Dojo.Eq("global", new List<string> { "x.x.x.x hit x.x.x.x", "no ip here" }, Sed(dojoIn, "s/[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+/x.x.x.x/g"));
Dojo.Eq("plain text, first only", new List<string> { "ba-aa" }, Sed(new List<string> { "aa-aa" }, "s/a/b/"));
